The *Candātherīgāthā* (Thig 5.12) is a short poetic text preserved in the *Therīgāthā* ("Verses of the Senior Nuns") within the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the five-verse section (*Pañcakanipāta*) of the collection and preserves the verses attributed to the elder nun (*therī*) Candā.

SuttaCentral records fifteen translations of the text in eleven modern languages, including English translations by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. No curatorial parallels in other early Buddhist canons or parallel Āgama literature are recorded by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus also reports no cross-language matches reaching a threshold score of 10 or greater in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus detects five matching text segments shared with the commentary on the collection, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0509a), with the longest continuous correspondence spanning verses §0.3–6.1 of the root text and §1811–1824 of the commentary (with 1,000 matched characters and a similarity rating of 0.92) [DharmaNexus].
